thesis: CDNA is a beta-2.5 stock that gapped to a 52-week high on earnings and has since given back about 14% (90.87 to 77.88), with a further pre-market dip to 76.85. Growth is decelerating (YoY about 52% to 39%, QoQ 12.1% to 5.6%) while valuation is rich (forward P/E 49.8, EV/EBITDA 151), and the headline profit is flattered by a probable one-off in Q2. The proposed 74.9 stop is only about 0.4 ATR from entry, so a whipsaw is likely, and the setup depends on a pullback hold that is still unconfirmed. The market regime is risk-off with QQQ below its 50- and 200-day averages and the 10-year yield at the 91st percentile, which hits high-beta, high-multiple names. A failed hold opens the gap-fill toward 64.6-70, and 13.9% short interest cuts both ways.
